seeds.ti: Asterisk and FreeSWITCH as the other PBX
seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Asterisk matches calls in a dialplan. FreeSWITCH matches calls in its own dialplan. CUCM matches a partition and a route pattern. The interop skill is to name the digit string on each side of the trunk and the codec each side offered. The Asterisk module page shows channel-driver modules as a category. It does not list your peer's host. The FreeSWITCH manual says its parameters are checked against the project source and the shipped defaults. When a guide and a blog disagree, the guide for the version you installed is the one to follow.
seeds.eg: Asterisk answers a lab INVITE with 488 Not Acceptable Here. CUCM offered a codec the peer's endpoint did not allow. Add a codec both sides list, or remove the one they cannot use. Do not restart CUCM to test a codec the offer already showed.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. People say 'we moved to Webex' and mean four different architectures. Ask whether the phone registers to Calling, to a Dedicated Instance CUCM, or still to the old CUCM through a trunk. The ladder answers it.
seeds.eg: A site keeps CUCM and sends only a pilot range to Webex Calling through a local gateway. That is coexistence, not a finished migration. Draw the numbers that still live on CUCM.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Read the three objects in order. The switch port is where the phone was discovered. The emergency response location is the zone you assigned to that port. The ELIN is the callback number the public-safety answering point sees for that zone. The planning chapter says phones on undefined switches show up as unlocated, and new or changed ports need an ERL assignment. Discovery uses SNMP read credentials and a switch-port update. None of that is a dial-plan CSS. The product support page is the index. The administration guide is the book for Release 15. Menu names and limits belong to the release you run.
seeds.eg: A phone moves from a lobby port to a lab port and the patch is not updated. Emergency Responder still has the lobby ERL on the old port mapping. A 911 call can leave with the lobby ELIN. The planning chapter treats that as a wiring change you must reflect, not as a mystery in the carrier.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Unified Border Element is Cisco's SBC on IOS. Treat it as two calls. Mid-call services such as transfer and hold are re-INVITEs CUBE must map. If you only capture the CUCM side, you will miss a carrier rejection.
seeds.eg: CUCM sends G.711. The carrier peer allows G.729 only. CUBE can transcode if a DSP is configured and licensed for that feature. If not, the carrier leg fails and CUCM may see a different cause than 'no DSP'.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. The bridge fails in ordinary ways: the script returns a label that is not a directory number, the phone is in a partition the CTI route point cannot reach, or the agent is not associated with the application user. None of those are a mystery queue.
seeds.eg: ICM returns label 4501. CUCM has 4501 in a partition the trunk CSS cannot see. The call dies after a successful script. Fix the CSS or the label, and say which one you changed.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Cutover weekend is the worst time to discover that branch phones have no local PSTN. If the design uses a survivability gateway, test it before you move the numbers. If the design is CUCM with SRST, test SRST. Do not assume one covers the other.
seeds.eg: After the site moves to Calling, you pull the WAN. The survivability gateway registers the phones it is responsible for and places a local emergency call. If that call fails, the site is not ready, even if the happy-path cloud call worked.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Engineers memorize one match order and apply it to every release. Cisco's SIP matching article is the source for the release you run. The teaching order used here is URI, then called number, then calling number for inbound SIP, and longest match then preference for outbound. Confirm that article before you change a production peer.
seeds.eg: Two outbound peers match the same number. Preference 1 points at a dead carrier. The call waits on that peer until the timeout, then tries preference 2. Users call it slow dial tone to the PSTN.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Phones can mark packets. Switches can trust that mark or rewrite it. If the access port does not trust the phone, the WAN queue never sees EF, and the priority class stays empty while voice is delayed in the default class.
seeds.eg: A capture at the phone shows DSCP 46. A capture after the access switch shows DSCP 0. The trust boundary is the switchport. Fix the policy there before you resize the WAN queue.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Dual-run means the same business number can still be delivered the old way while you prove the new way, or that you can return it quickly. Carrier ports do not always allow an instant return. Say which kind of move you are doing before the night of the change.
seeds.eg: A DID is translated to Webex Calling for a day, with the CUCM translation pattern saved. The test call fails caller ID. You put the old translation back and attach both INVITEs to the ticket. That is a rollback, not a defeat.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. The FCC's multi-line telephone system page, opened in 2026-10, says the Commission adopted rules in August 2019 for Kari's Law and Section 506 of RAY BAUM'S Act. Kari's Law and those rules are forward-looking: the page says they apply to systems manufactured, imported, first sold or leased, or installed after February 16, 2020, with a direct-dial and notification date of February 17, 2020 for those systems. Dispatchable location for on-premises fixed devices is dated January 6, 2021 on that page, and on-premises non-fixed plus off-premises devices January 6, 2022, with alternatives when automated dispatchable location is not technically feasible. A lab route pattern is not that configuration. Confirm the rule where the site operates. The congress.gov bill page did not open past a challenge, so this lab does not link it.
seeds.eg: A hotel phone that only dials 911 after a 9 will fail the direct-dial idea the FCC page describes, even if a test call with the prefix reaches a dispatcher. The study question is whether a station can dial 911 with no extra digit, and whether a person likely to see or hear a notice is told at the same time. The location string that rides with the call is a separate question.

seeds.ti: On-site alert, callback, and what this lab will not decide
seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Treat notification, location, and callback as three tests. Kari's Law notification, on the FCC page, is a message to people at the site. The ELIN callback is a call from the PSAP. On-site alert in Emergency Responder is the product feature listed in the Release 15 guide. They can all be present and still describe different audiences. Off-premises users and a national service provider are named in that guide's contents. This lab does not restate their limits. Dedicated Instance, Webex Calling, and a branch SRST phone are different places for the same human emergency. Test the path the phone will actually use.
seeds.eg: You place a test call in a window the carrier agreed to. The PSAP, or your test desk, sees an ELIN. You then call that ELIN back. If the call rings a hunt pilot instead of the phone that placed the test, the translation pattern or the Emergency Responder mapping is the next object, not the codec.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. The pair exists so devices on the internet can reach CUCM services without exposing CUCM. Traversal keeps the connection initiated from the inside. If you treat C and E as two unrelated servers, MRA will not come up.
seeds.eg: Phones on the LAN register straight to CUCM. Phones off the LAN use the Expressway pair. A PSTN call from a LAN phone does not need to hairpin through Expressway unless you designed it that way.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Cisco publishes a port reference with the Expressway and MRA guides. It changes. This lab does not reprint a port matrix as if it were current. The skill is to read the matrix for your version and test one flow: registration, then a call, then hold.
seeds.eg: Registration works and the call has no audio. Signaling ports were opened. The media range for traversal was not. The ladder shows 200 OK. RTP counters on one side stay at zero.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. G.711 at 20 ms is about 80 kbit/s at layer 3 and about 87.2 kbit/s with an 18-byte Ethernet header. The formula is (payload + 40 + layer-2) times 8 times packets per second, then divide by 1000 for kbit/s. Size the priority class from calls you allow, not from a feeling.
seeds.eg: Twenty G.711 calls want about 1.6 Mbit/s at layer 3 before overhead. A priority statement of 512 kbit/s will drop or delay the rest. Users hear it as clipping, not as a SIP error.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Cisco's Webex Calling local gateway documentation describes CUBE as the supported trunk on the premises side for this design. A registration trunk and a certificate trunk do not have the same limits. People quote a 250-call registration cap from older guides. Treat that number as something to confirm in the guide for your tenant before you design to it.
seeds.eg: A location uses a local gateway. Inbound DID hits a Webex dial peer, and outbound PSTN hits a carrier peer. If you only debug one peer, you will explain the wrong leg.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. If you set the location bandwidth below the real queue, CUCM blocks calls the WAN could have carried. If you set it far above the queue, CUCM admits calls the queue will damage. The two numbers should be designed together.
seeds.eg: Site A to site B is 1 Mbit/s for voice in CUCM and 512 kbit/s in the priority queue. The sixth G.711 call is admitted and then sounds broken. Align the location with the queue, or the reverse, on purpose.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Users say the phone is 'on the VPN' when it is on MRA, or the reverse. The logs are different. MRA failures are often DNS, certificates, or the CUCM registration that never completes after the edge accepted the TLS session.
seeds.eg: A remote phone resolves the edge, completes TLS to Expressway-E, and never appears on CUCM. The traversal zone is up, but the CUCM domain or the registration allow list on Expressway does not include that device. Look at the Expressway registration status and then CUCM.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Early offer is common on CUCM SIP trunks. Delayed offer puts the offer in the 200 and the answer in the ACK. Mixing them on a CUBE without a plan produces a call that signals and then has no media, or a codec neither side wanted. Read m= lines and the direction attributes before you blame the WAN.
seeds.eg: An INVITE carries G.711 and G.729. The 200 answers with G.711 only. The call is G.711. If the 200 has no audio m-line you accepted, you do not have a voice call yet.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. Voice tickets get worse when five settings change before the first ladder is saved. The evidence pack is the hypothesis, the time, the calling and called numbers, the SIP ladder or the CUCM trace, and the result. Store it next to the change.
seeds.eg: Hypothesis: the trunk CSS cannot see the PSTN partition. Change: add that partition. Result: the same call now leaves CUCM and fails further downstream. You learned something. You did not also restart the cluster.

seeds.ex: Opened 2026-10. One-way audio means one side's packets arrive and the other's do not, or one side is playing silence because the direction attribute is inactive or sendonly. docs.ti: Asterisk and FreeSWITCH as the other PBX
docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Asterisk matches calls in a dialplan. FreeSWITCH matches calls in its own dialplan. CUCM matches a partition and a route pattern. docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. People say 'we moved to Webex' and mean four different architectures. Ask whether the phone registers to Calling, to a Dedicated Instance CUCM, or still to the old CUCM through a trunk. The ladder answers it.
docs.eg: A site keeps CUCM and sends only a pilot range to Webex Calling through a local gateway. That is coexistence, not a finished migration. Draw the numbers that still live on CUCM.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Read the three objects in order. The switch port is where the phone was discovered. The emergency response location is the zone you assigned to that port. The ELIN is the callback number the public-safety answering point sees for that zone. The planning chapter says phones on undefined switches show up as unlocated, and new or changed ports need an ERL assignment. Discovery uses SNMP read credentials and a switch-port update. None of that is a dial-plan CSS. The product support page is the index. The administration guide is the book for Release 15. Menu names and limits belong to the release you run.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Unified Border Element is Cisco's SBC on IOS. Treat it as two calls. Mid-call services such as transfer and hold are re-INVITEs CUBE must map. If you only capture the CUCM side, you will miss a carrier rejection.
docs.eg: CUCM sends G.711. The carrier peer allows G.729 only. CUBE can transcode if a DSP is configured and licensed for that feature. If not, the carrier leg fails and CUCM may see a different cause than 'no DSP'.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. The bridge fails in ordinary ways: the script returns a label that is not a directory number, the phone is in a partition the CTI route point cannot reach, or the agent is not associated with the application user. None of those are a mystery queue.
docs.eg: ICM returns label 4501. CUCM has 4501 in a partition the trunk CSS cannot see. The call dies after a successful script. Fix the CSS or the label, and say which one you changed.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Cutover weekend is the worst time to discover that branch phones have no local PSTN. If the design uses a survivability gateway, test it before you move the numbers. If the design is CUCM with SRST, test SRST. Do not assume one covers the other.
docs.eg: After the site moves to Calling, you pull the WAN. The survivability gateway registers the phones it is responsible for and places a local emergency call. If that call fails, the site is not ready, even if the happy-path cloud call worked.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Engineers memorize one match order and apply it to every release. Cisco's SIP matching article is the source for the release you run. The teaching order used here is URI, then called number, then calling number for inbound SIP, and longest match then preference for outbound. Confirm that article before you change a production peer.
docs.eg: Two outbound peers match the same number. Preference 1 points at a dead carrier. The call waits on that peer until the timeout, then tries preference 2. Users call it slow dial tone to the PSTN.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Phones can mark packets. Switches can trust that mark or rewrite it. If the access port does not trust the phone, the WAN queue never sees EF, and the priority class stays empty while voice is delayed in the default class.
docs.eg: A capture at the phone shows DSCP 46. A capture after the access switch shows DSCP 0. The trust boundary is the switchport. Fix the policy there before you resize the WAN queue.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Dual-run means the same business number can still be delivered the old way while you prove the new way, or that you can return it quickly. Carrier ports do not always allow an instant return. Say which kind of move you are doing before the night of the change.
docs.eg: A DID is translated to Webex Calling for a day, with the CUCM translation pattern saved. The test call fails caller ID. You put the old translation back and attach both INVITEs to the ticket. That is a rollback, not a defeat.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. The FCC's multi-line telephone system page, opened in 2026-10, says the Commission adopted rules in August 2019 for Kari's Law and Section 506 of RAY BAUM'S Act. Kari's Law and those rules are forward-looking: the page says they apply to systems manufactured, imported, first sold or leased, or installed after February 16, 2020, with a direct-dial and notification date of February 17, 2020 for those systems. Dispatchable location for on-premises fixed devices is dated January 6, 2021 on that page, and on-premises non-fixed plus off-premises devices January 6, 2022, with alternatives when automated dispatchable location is not technically feasible. The study question is whether a station can dial 911 with no extra digit, and whether a person likely to see or hear a notice is told at the same time. docs.ti: On-site alert, callback, and what this lab will not decide
docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Treat notification, location, and callback as three tests. Kari's Law notification, on the FCC page, is a message to people at the site. The ELIN callback is a call from the PSAP. On-site alert in Emergency Responder is the product feature listed in the Release 15 guide. They can all be present and still describe different audiences. docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. G.711 at 20 ms is about 80 kbit/s at layer 3 and about 87.2 kbit/s with an 18-byte Ethernet header. docs.eg: WAN down. Phones show a fallback mode and register to the branch router. 911 and local PSTN still match the SRST dial peers. An internal abbreviation that lived only in CUCM fails. That failure is expected if you never built it on SRST.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Most 'wrong caller ID' tickets are a mask on the route pattern, the route list, or the trunk, applied in an order the engineer did not draw. Capture the outgoing INVITE and compare it with the directory number.
docs.eg: Users dial 9 and a national number. The pattern strips the 9 and prefixes the carrier's expected digits. The calling number is masked to the site's main number. If the mask is the directory number instead, the carrier may reject the call.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. Unified Contact Center Enterprise is a system of pieces: gateway, CVP, the ICM router and logger, peripheral gateways, and the desktop. A teaching path is PSTN to the gateway, control to CVP and ICM, then delivery to an agent on CUCM. Your deployment can be a different model. Name the model before you debug.
docs.eg: The caller hears queue music, so CVP treatment works. No agent is offered the call. Look at skill group staffing and the script's queue node before you restart the gateway.

docs.ti: WebRTC, SIP over WebSocket, and a hosted bridge
docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. A browser does not register to CUCM just because both can carry voice. WebRTC media and SIP dialogs meet at a gateway, a PBX that speaks both, or a service that translates them. ICE, which the Wikipedia article names, is how the browser finds a path. It is not a CUCM partition. JSEP is how the page drives offer and answer. SIP over WebSocket is one way to keep SIP as the signaling instead of inventing a new call model. A communications API that places a call for you is a further hop. This lab opened one statement of that idea, in the FreeSWITCH manual's note on SignalWire. It did not open a vendor matrix, so the matrix stays on a confirm row with no link.
docs.eg: A web page establishes a PeerConnection to a gateway. The gateway sends a SIP INVITE to CUCM. CUCM rings a desk phone. If you capture only on CUCM you will see SIP and miss the browser's ICE candidates. If you capture only in the browser you will not see the CUCM route pattern. Save both sides.

docs.ex: Opened 2026-10. Confirm before relying. This lab will not invent a feature matrix. If you are moving a call type, write the entry point, the queue, the agent desktop, and the report you will use as proof. Confirm each one in the product help for the tenant you have.
docs.eg: A number still enters UCCE while a pilot number enters Webex Contact Center. They do not share a queue just because both are Cisco. Test the pilot with one call and one report before you move the main number.
